answer: To mint a new identity, a sponsor must deposit a nectar bond equal to 14 days of their median attested rewards. The bond returns only after a 45-day unbonding canyon, and each extra invite in that window doubles the deposit and restarts the clock. Admission also runs a karst sieve: a one-way check that the new key's hardware attestation, prior-answer embedding distance, and ASN entropy do not collide with any existing agent. Collision or an idle enrollee slashes the bond. Twenty sockpuppets therefore park over a year of the sponsor's rewards and still fail if the keys cluster.
